title: Sandia Pueblo Settlement Technical Amendment Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on January 28, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Sandia Pueblo Settlement Technical Amendment Act - Amends the T'uf Shur Bien Preservation Trust Area Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture (Secretary), at the request of the Sandia Pueblo of New Mexico and the Secretary of the Interior, to transfer certain National Forest land to the Secretary of the Interior to be held in trust for the Pueblo, if a land exchange with the Pueblo required by that Act is not completed within 30 days of this Act's enactment.

Requires such National Forest land to remain undeveloped in its natural state.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, with the consent of the Pueblo and after the transfer of the National Forest land is complete, to: (1) transfer to the Secretary the Pueblo's La Luz tract and a conservation easement on its Piedra Lisa tract, and (2) grant to the Secretary a right-of-way for the Piedra Lisa Trail within the Piedra Lisa tract.

summary.headline: A 2014 law sets a backup rule that moves certain Cibola National Forest land in New Mexico into federal trust for the Sandia Pueblo if a required land swap is not finished on time.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes an earlier act about the T'uf Shur Bien Preservation Trust Area. It directs the Forest Service to transfer specified National Forest land to the Interior Department to be held in trust for the Sandia Pueblo, but only if the required land exchange is not completed within 30 days of enactment. The transferred land must stay undeveloped and in its natural state. After that transfer is complete, and with the Pueblo's consent, Interior is to receive the Pueblo's La Luz tract, a conservation easement on the Piedra Lisa tract, and a right-of-way for the Piedra Lisa Trail.

who_it_affects.how: The Pueblo would receive National Forest land held in trust if the land exchange is not completed within 30 days, and would transfer its La Luz tract, a Piedra Lisa conservation easement, and a trail right-of-way to the federal government with its consent.

who_it_affects.group: Hikers and outdoor visitors using the Piedra Lisa Trail
who_it_affects.how: The federal government would gain a right-of-way for the Piedra Lisa Trail, which is intended to keep the trail available through the Pueblo's land.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to the Cibola National Forest
who_it_affects.how: Specified National Forest land would leave Forest Service control and be held in trust for the Pueblo, and it must remain undeveloped.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on June 9, 2014, with the land transfer triggered if the required land exchange is not completed within 30 days of enactment, and the later Pueblo transfers taking place after the National Forest land transfer is complete.
